excludes: rich surfaces (3D, audio, widget) — design steps 3-4, conditional on the F13.6 Q1 decision; not in this shell
frame kinds the contract does not name — the shell adds none and privately extends none
offline reading — not claimed; that is the browser shell's slice-1 surface (issue #10927). This shell presents a live session
mobile-native presentation — deferred to the v2 rung (issue #6297)
posture: local-first: the shell is a presentation client of a world host reached directly over iroh; it hosts no world and implements no hosted or quota surface

presentation.error: not presented as content: an error frame refuses the session and surfaces as a session failure
presentation.events: retained as a bounded tail and summarized for presentation (chat_posted, region_changed, object_changed, input_applied, program_changed, system_event)
presentation.screen: styled per-cell grid with the xterm-256 palette (src/render.rs)
presentation.semantic_diff: retained as a bounded tail and rendered as text (agent profile, contract revision 11)
presentation.surface_less_view: the legacy `data` text fallback, the same rule the terminal shell presents
presentation.text_and_form: deterministic text projection; form surfaces render as widget rows with their actions, answered with form_result

providers.declaration: named in the provider_offer frame at session start; the grant is local and per world, bounded by the F12.4 provider manifest (id_caps::world_caps::CLIENT_FILE_READ_MANIFEST) composed by minimum with the shell's local bounds — a provider only ever narrows the session
providers.execution: reads only beneath the granted root: Linux uses openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH; non-Linux targets canonicalize the requested path and verify it remains beneath the root before opening. Every request is answered with a provider_reply frame and recorded in the shell's local audit

recorded_for: shells v1 native target statements (Linux #10928, macOS #12817); terms per doc/2026-11-10T20-40-00Z_design_more_shells_v1 (issue #6296), section 2 and 'The one gate'
